answer: Each task instance is derived from a specified future drand quicknet round: its threshold-BLS pulse is unpredictable before release and publicly verifiable afterward. An agent commits first, then reveals work bound to that pulse, so cached answers and offline farms cannot prepare task-specific proofs across many identities. Domain-separated inputs such as vine, marble, and timber prevent replay; beacon randomness limits precomputation, while quotas or stake must still constrain parallel Sybil attempts.
